claims.statement: A kinematical classical system is a finite-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with a designated algebra of smooth real-valued observables.
A Hamiltonian system is a kinematical system whose state manifold carries a symplectic form and a Hamiltonian function.
Admissible processes contain identity maps and are closed under typed composition.
Kinematical systems with admissible smooth processes form a category.
Cartesian-product parallel composition makes the category of finite-dimensional smooth systems and smooth maps symmetric monoidal, up to the standard canonical diffeomorphisms.
The direct-sum two-form on a product of symplectic manifolds is symplectic.
For an additive Hamiltonian on a product symplectic manifold, the Hamiltonian vector field is the product of the component Hamiltonian vector fields.
The flow of a noninteracting additive composite factorizes into the product of the component flows wherever both component flows exist.

Within the paper's definitions, compositional closure separates into four logically independent layers: kinematical product, observable embeddings, dynamical factorization, and empirical compositionality; none of the first three entails the fourth.
A mathematical state represents a physical preparation only after an empirically supported representation map and an explicit resolution criterion are supplied.
Finite-dimensional Hamiltonian mechanics models conservative classical systems by symplectic state spaces and Hamiltonian flows.
The illustrative two-particle model treats the pair's joint state space as the Cartesian product of the individual phase spaces.
A useful general empirical theory of composition can be organized by lax symmetric-monoidal realization maps from mathematical systems to operational preparation-and-measurement structures.

claims.statement: A typed presentation of a physical theory is one in which every symbol carries a declared type, every judgement carries an epistemic label, and no derivation rule permits a judgement of label l to be inferred unless the inference is licensed for l; in particular an Assumption may be a premise but never the conclusion of a proof, and an Empirical statement may not be the conclusion of a purely mathematical derivation.

A physical theory object is a tuple T = (K, D, I, E): K a kinematic layer (states with distinguished structure plus a commutative R-algebra Obs of observables), D a dynamical layer (a one-parameter family of structure-preserving endomorphisms with its infinitesimal generator), I an interface layer (a finite tuple of port observables), and E an empirical interpretation layer (a triple (P, rho, epsilon) of laboratory procedures, an assignment of dimensioned observables in a finitely generated free abelian dimension group, and stated uncertainties).
Layer separation: E is not a function of (K, D, I). No theorem of the paper derives any component of E from the other three layers, and no assignment of E is claimed to be canonical.

All manifolds are smooth, second countable, Hausdorff and finite dimensional; all maps are smooth; all vector fields are complete unless stated otherwise. Field theory, infinite-dimensional analysis, general relativity, quantum mechanics, quantum field theory and theory-space geometry are outside scope and appear only as boundary tests. No new experimental claim is made.

A symplectic manifold is a pair (M, omega) with omega a 2-form that is nondegenerate (the map v -> omega(v, .) is a bundle isomorphism TM -> T*M) and closed (d omega = 0); nondegeneracy forces even dimension, and Obs := C^infty(M, R).
For each H in C^infty(M) there is exactly one vector field X_H with iota_{X_H} omega = dH. Proved by inverting the smooth bundle isomorphism omega-flat pointwise and using injectivity for uniqueness.

For every x in M and every v in T_xM there is f in C^infty(M) with X_f(x) = v. Proved by choosing a linear function in a chart with prescribed differential at x and cutting it off with a bump function.

With the conventions iota_{X_f} omega = df and {f,g} := omega(X_f, X_g), the identity d omega(X_f, X_g, X_h) = 2 Jac(f,g,h) holds for all f, g, h. Consequently d omega = 0 if and only if the bracket satisfies the Jacobi identity. Proved from the intrinsic exterior-derivative formula together with X_{ {a,b} } = -[X_a, X_b], and converted to a pointwise statement using pointwise surjectivity.

Non-example: on R^3 the bivector Pi = x1 d1^d2 + x3 d2^d3 + x1 d3^d1 defines a bilinear, antisymmetric, Leibniz bracket with {x1,x2} = x1, {x2,x3} = x3, {x3,x1} = x1 whose Jacobiator equals Jac(x1,x2,x3) = x1, not identically zero. Hence bilinearity, antisymmetry and the Leibniz rule do not imply Jacobi.

For a bilinear, antisymmetric, Leibniz bracket and X_H := {., H}, the operator X_H is a derivation of the bracket for all f, g if and only if Jac(f, g, H) = 0 for all f, g. In particular Poisson's theorem (the bracket of two constants of motion is a constant of motion) holds under Jacobi and is unavailable in the non-Jacobi example.

Darboux's theorem: every symplectic manifold admits local coordinates in which omega = sum_i dq^i ^ dp_i, so the kinematic layer has no local invariants beyond dimension. Attributed to Abraham-Marsden, Arnold and McDuff-Salamon; not re-derived here.

Because Darboux's theorem removes all local kinematic invariants, the interface and empirical layers cannot be dispensed with: if the kinematic layer alone fixed physical content, all 2n-dimensional classical systems would be locally physically identical, which no laboratory reports. This is indirect internal evidence for the layer-separation axiom, not a proof of it.

Dynamical axioms on a symplectic (M, omega): (D1) the dynamics is a smooth R-action (determinism and reversibility); (D2) each time map preserves omega; (D3) the action is autonomous. These remain assumptions wherever used and are not converted into theorems by the reconstruction theorem.

Under the dynamical axioms, the generator X satisfies: (i) iota_X omega is closed; (ii) X is locally Hamiltonian; (iii) if H^1_dR(M) = 0 then X = X_H globally for an H unique up to an additive constant per connected component. Proved via d/dt of the pullback, Cartan's magic formula, and the Poincare lemma.

Non-example: on the compact symplectic manifold (T^2, d theta_1 ^ d theta_2) the field X = d/d theta_1 satisfies (D1)-(D3) and has iota_X omega = d theta_2, closed but not exact (its integral over a generating loop is 1). Hence X is locally but not globally Hamiltonian, and the cohomological hypothesis in part (iii) of the reconstruction theorem is not removable.
Under the dynamical axioms the flow preserves the volume form omega^n/n!, because pullback is an algebra homomorphism for the wedge product.

The product form omega_oplus = pi_1^* omega_1 + pi_2^* omega_2 is symplectic on M_1 x M_2, both projections are Poisson maps, and pullbacks of observables from the two factors Poisson-commute; so the parts of a free composite remain identifiable inside it.

For the linear position-position interconnection with coupling matrices C12 and C21, the flow preserves the product symplectic form omega_oplus if and only if C21 = C12^T; in that case the composite is Hamiltonian with interaction term H_int = (q1)^T C12 q2. Proved by computing d(iota_Y omega_oplus) = sum_{a,b} ((C21)_{ba} - (C12)_{ab}) dq1_a ^ dq2_b.

The coupled linear field has trace zero for all C12, C21, so its flow preserves Lebesgue volume even when C12 is not equal to C21^T, where by the reciprocity theorem it does not preserve omega_oplus. This is an explicit witness that the converse of Liouville's corollary fails for 2n >= 4; the distinction itself is classical.

For one degree of freedom per factor, the coupled flow preserves some split-respecting symplectic form defined near the origin if and only if c12 = 0 exactly when c21 = 0. When both are nonzero, Omega = c21 omega_1 (+) c12 omega_2 works; when exactly one vanishes no such form exists. Proved by evaluating invariance at the fixed point, reducing to symmetry of Omega_0 A with Omega_0 = diag(a1 J, a2 J), which is equivalent to the single scalar condition a1 c12 = a2 c21 with a1 a2 nonzero. The argument does not assume Omega is constant.

A pair of one-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian objects coupled unidirectionally (c12 = 0, c21 nonzero) is not a Hamiltonian theory object over the given decomposition, for any symplectic structure compatible with that decomposition.

Hamiltonicity is not a property of a vector field but a typed structure relative to a decomposition. Insisting on the parts' own symplectic forms makes composability exactly reciprocity; relaxing to any split-respecting form buys back precisely the bidirectional non-reciprocal couplings, at the cost of rescaling each subsystem's energy scale, and buys back nothing for unidirectional coupling.

Unidirectional and non-reciprocal couplings are realized in the laboratory (servo feedback loops, optical isolators and circulators, engineered non-reciprocal mechanical and photonic media); Onsager's reciprocal relations identify the near-equilibrium regime where reciprocity is recovered and, through magnetic-field and Coriolis sign reversals, where it is not. Asserted as existing practice, not as a new measurement.

If J is a momentum map for a symplectic G-action and H is G-invariant, then each component J_xi is a constant of motion for X_H. Proved in one line from invariance of H and the bracket identity X_g f = {f, g}.

The typed Noether proposition is the Hamiltonian form of Noether's first theorem; translation, rotation and time-translation invariance yield conservation of linear momentum, angular momentum and energy. Attributed to Noether 1918 and Marsden-Ratiu; treated as established, not re-derived from experiment.

The Noether proposition concerns only K and D. That the conserved quantity J_xi is the momentum an experimenter measures is a statement about E and is not entailed by the proposition; conflating the two is the most common practical violation of the non-conflation rule.

For oscillators h_m = (R^2, dq^dp, H_m = p^2/2m + (1/2) m omega_0^2 q^2, port A = q): (i) all h_m with fixed omega_0 are isomorphic after forgetting ports, via the symplectomorphism (q,p) -> (alpha q, alpha^{-1} p) with alpha = sqrt(m/m'); (ii) they are isomorphic as port objects only if m = m', proved by showing port preservation forces psi(q,p) = (q, p + h(q)) and then comparing p^2 coefficients; (iii) the distinction is empirically realized, since a calibrated drive of amplitude F gives steady-state port amplitude F/(m(omega_0^2 - Omega^2)). Hence mathematical isomorphism of the closed-system layers does not determine physical equivalence.

There exist port objects h, h' that are non-isomorphic in Ham_port whose images are isomorphic in Ham. Isomorphism in Ham is therefore a strictly coarser equivalence on interpreted systems, and the forgetful functor does not reflect isomorphism of objects.

The pendulum object on T*S^1 and the harmonic object on R^2 are not isomorphic in Ham (T*S^1 is not simply connected while R^2 is), yet on the window of amplitudes theta_0 <= 0.12 rad no period measurement at relative uncertainty 10^{-3} separates them, since the leading correction theta_0^2/16 <= 9.0e-4. Hence empirical equivalence on a window does not imply isomorphism.
The pendulum amplitude correction T(theta_0)/T_0 - 1 approximately equals theta_0^2/16 is a standard, repeatedly confirmed laboratory result, cited as established rather than measured anew.

The claim that two theories are the same is ill-typed unless indexed by which layers are compared and by which window and uncertainty are in force. In the typed presentation both indices are components of the object, so the ill-typed statement cannot be formed.

For gamma > 0 the linearly damped oscillator field on R^2 admits no invariant symplectic form. Proved by evaluating invariance at the fixed point at the origin, where det D phi_t(0) = exp(-2 gamma t), forcing the density rho(0) = 0 and contradicting nondegeneracy.

The damped oscillator has two standard repairs that are empirically distinguishable and must not be treated as one move: enlarging K to a system-plus-environment Hamiltonian object (predicting fluctuations and recurrences alongside damping), or giving up autonomy with a time-dependent Hamiltonian on the same R^2 (predicting damping with no fluctuation). Which is adequate is an empirical question about E; port-Hamiltonian theory formalises a third route via resistive and source ports.

Non-examples in the kinematic layer: S^6 is almost symplectic (an octonionic almost complex structure with a compatible metric gives a nondegenerate 2-form) but carries no symplectic form, since H^2_dR(S^6) = 0 while a closed symplectic 2n-manifold requires a nonzero class; S^4 admits no almost complex structure, hence not even a nondegenerate 2-form; and no odd-dimensional manifold admits a nondegenerate 2-form, since skew forms on odd-dimensional real vector spaces are singular.

Boundary tests recorded but not pursued: constrained systems need presymplectic or Dirac-constraint machinery; in infinite dimensions Darboux's theorem fails in general so the reconstruction does not transfer verbatim; quantization is not a functor on the full Poisson algebra by the Groenewold-van Hove obstruction; and Poisson manifolds with their symplectic-leaf decomposition are the correct kinematic type at nonconstant rank. None of these is settled here.

An observation falsifies the claim that h realizes S on window W if it is a run in W and some procedure reads a value differing from the h-prediction for its assigned observable by more than the stated uncertainty.

Each dynamical assumption has a distinct empirical signature: (D1) fails on systematically divergent outcomes from identical preparations or non-solution time-reversed runs; (D2) fails on measured non-reciprocal linear response at a fixed decomposition or on shrinking phase-space area, with volume preservation in 2n >= 4 a strictly weaker test that cannot substitute; (D3) fails on response depending on absolute laboratory time beyond stated drift; and global existence of H fails with all of (D1)-(D3) intact when H^1_dR(M) is nonzero.

The Newtonian two-body object for Sun-Mercury leaves an anomalous perihelion residual of about 43 arcseconds per century, accounted for by general relativity. This falsifies the Newtonian object at that precision on that window, not the Hamiltonian type, since the replacement theory also admits Hamiltonian formulations; separating domain failure from structural failure is a function of the typed presentation.

Programmes fitting dynamical laws to trajectory data (sparse regression over a candidate library; neural parameterizations constrained to be Hamiltonian) presuppose K and I and estimate only D. They do not, and do not claim to, supply E.

Conjecture: if a smooth vector field on an open subset of R^{2n} has a nondegenerate equilibrium at x_0 and, for a fixed decomposition into n port pairs, a fully reciprocal linear response matrix at x_0, then it admits an invariant split-respecting symplectic form near x_0, unique up to a nonzero scalar per factor. Settled here only for the specific coupling family with two factors of one degree of freedom each; the general case is open and a counterexample would be as informative as a proof.

A Haskell module encoding the linear fragment was executed under GHC and verified the reciprocity and split-obstruction theorems on five instances: (0.3, 0.3) and (0.0, 0.0) preserve the product form; (0.3, 0.1) and (0.3, -0.2) fail the product form but admit the rescaled split form; (0.0, 0.3) fails both. Output is reproduced verbatim in the paper. This checks instances, not the theorems in general: it is a test, not a proof.

Assessment against the founding thesis: the reconstruction is precise and compatible with established mechanics, and the layer discipline held (no result about K or D was used to derive anything about E). The framework earned one non-obvious statement, the unidirectional-coupling obstruction, which constrains rather than vindicates the word compositional: the word does real work only if the admissible couplings are stated, namely reciprocal for strict composition and bidirectional for composition up to energy-scale rescaling. Not shown: that the four-layer typing is the only or best one, or that E admits a general formal definition beyond the finite-procedure form.

result.summary: A 10-page arXiv-style LaTeX paper reconstructing finite-dimensional Hamiltonian mechanics as a four-layer typed theory object (kinematic, dynamical, interface/ports, empirical interpretation), with a layer-separation axiom forbidding derivation of the empirical layer from the mathematical ones. Three proved results anchor the paper: (1) a reconstruction theorem deriving X = X_H from determinism, symplectic structure preservation, autonomy and H^1_dR(M) = 0, with a T^2 counterexample showing the cohomological hypothesis is not removable; (2) a composition theorem — the linearly coupled pair preserves the product symplectic form iff C21 = C12^T, and (for one degree of freedom per factor, completely classified) preserves some split-respecting symplectic form iff c12 and c21 vanish together, making unidirectional coupling a sharp, unrepairable obstruction to composition; (3) a non-conflation theorem showing isomorphism in the closed-system category is neither sufficient (oscillators of equal frequency and unequal mass) nor necessary (pendulum vs harmonic within a stated uncertainty window) for empirical equivalence. Non-examples cover a non-Jacobi bracket, the damped oscillator (no invariant symplectic form on R^2, proved at the fixed point), S^6 and S^4, and odd dimension. Falsification signatures are given per assumption, boundary tests are recorded but not pursued, and a Haskell appendix executed under GHC checks the composition theorems on instances. Compilation is clean at 10 pages with zero undefined references; all 21 bibliography entries are cited and six bibliographic identities (including all four pilot candidates) were verified against publisher or repository records.
result.title: Hamiltonian Reconstruction as a Physical Theory Object: Finite-dimensional classical mechanics as a typed, composable, empirically interpreted structure
unresolved_questions: Conjecture 'Local reconstruction from reciprocity' is open: does full linear-response reciprocity at a nondegenerate equilibrium, for a fixed decomposition into n port pairs, imply existence of an invariant split-respecting symplectic form near that equilibrium? The paper settles only the two-factor, one-degree-of-freedom coupling family.

The complete classification of split-respecting invariant symplectic forms is proved only for one degree of freedom per factor, where every 2x2 skew block is forced to be a multiple of J. For n_i > 1 the paper proves only the sufficient condition C21^T proportional to C12 within the restricted family a1 omega_1 (+) a2 omega_2; the general classification over arbitrary symplectic forms on each factor is not settled.
Whether the four-layer typing (K, D, I, E) is canonical or merely one workable choice is not established; the paper labels this an interpretation, not a theorem.

Whether the empirical interpretation layer E admits a general formal definition beyond the finite-procedure triple (P, rho, epsilon) used here, in particular one that handles statistical outcome distributions rather than deterministic readings with tolerances.

Whether the composition obstruction has an analogue for nonlinear interconnections, and whether unidirectional coupling remains obstructed when the port structure is allowed to vary smoothly over the state space.

How the typed presentation interacts with constrained (presymplectic/Dirac) systems and with Poisson manifolds of nonconstant rank, both of which are excluded by the finite-dimensional symplectic scope assumption.

claims.statement: An empirical realization of a mathematical model relative to a protocol consists of a target, preparation map, measurement kernels, calibration conventions, and an error model satisfying a stated adequacy criterion.

The paper assumes finite-dimensional smooth state spaces, specified admissible preparations and interventions, and probabilistic measurement kernels; it does not assert that every physical system admits this representation.
Observational equivalence relative to a fixed protocol is an equivalence relation.

Every protocol factors uniquely through the quotient of model histories by protocol-relative observational equivalence, and this quotient is the maximal empirical content recoverable from that protocol.

A mathematical isomorphism yields observational equivalence only when the empirical interpretation is transported compatibly; without that condition mathematical equivalence does not imply physical equivalence.
For any finite set of sampled times, a smooth perturbation of a deterministic trajectory can agree at every sampled time yet disagree elsewhere, demonstrating finite-data underdetermination.
The relativistic kinetic energy converges to the Newtonian kinetic energy uniformly on compact momentum sets as c tends to infinity, but not uniformly on the full momentum line.
Harmonic-oscillator trajectories converge to free-particle trajectories on every bounded time interval as frequency tends to zero, while the convergence fails uniformly over all time.

Under a fixed protocol and error criterion, a realized model is falsified by an accepted datum exactly when that datum lies outside the model's protocol-indexed acceptance region; equivalent models have identical falsification status only when equivalence preserves that full acceptance region.
Empirical realization is protocol-relative and corrigible, rather than an intrinsic property of a bare mathematical structure.

A useful compositional empirical theory should require interpretation maps to respect composition up to quantified experimental tolerance; the adequacy of this requirement beyond finite-dimensional classical mechanics remains open.
